title: Categorical trace is invariant under an intertwining isomorphism
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided monoidal category with unit $\mathbf 1$, and let $P,Q\in\mathcal C$ each have a chosen right dual, with categorical trace defined by evaluation, braiding and coevaluation as in [sk-d-trace]. Let $u:P\to P$, $v:Q\to Q$, and $a:P\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ satisfy $a\circ u=v\circ a$. Then $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal C}(u)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal C}(v)$ in $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)$.

source.place: Part (3), final sentence invoking conjugacy invariance; abstract braided-category form implemented in lean/WeilConjectures/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Rigid/Braided.lean:92–96, CategoryTheory.MonoidalCategory.trace_eq_of_iso.

proof.text: Write $\eta_B,\varepsilon_B$ for the chosen coevaluation and evaluation, and $\beta_{B,B^\vee}$ for the forward braiding, for $B=P,Q$. Thus [sk-d-trace] gives $\operatorname{tr}(z)=\varepsilon_B\circ\beta_{B,B^\vee}\circ(z\otimes1_{B^\vee})\circ\eta_B$. Put $g=a:P\to Q$ and $h=u\circ a^{-1}:Q\to P$. The inverse identities give $h\circ g=u$, while the intertwining hypothesis gives $g\circ h=a\circ u\circ a^{-1}=v\circ a\circ a^{-1}=v$.

source.place: Part (3), final sentence invoking conjugacy invariance; explicit agent expansion of the dual-mate calculation in lean/WeilConjectures/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Rigid/Braided.lean:80–96.

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-right-dual-mate-identities] with $X=P$, $Y=Q$, $f=g$ and exactly the right duals chosen in the statement. It supplies $t:Q^\vee\to P^\vee$ with $(g\otimes1_{P^\vee})\circ\eta_P=(1_Q\otimes t)\circ\eta_Q$ and $\varepsilon_P\circ(t\otimes1_P)=\varepsilon_Q\circ(1_{Q^\vee}\otimes g)$. The only hypotheses are the two chosen right dualities; both are given.

source.place: Part (3), final sentence invoking conjugacy invariance; explicit agent expansion of the dual-mate calculation in lean/WeilConjectures/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Rigid/Braided.lean:80–96.

proof.text:
Expand the trace by [sk-d-trace], substitute $u=h\circ g$, and use the coevaluation equation from [lem-zl-right-dual-mate-identities]. Bifunctoriality of tensor gives the explicit equality
$$\operatorname{tr}(u)=\varepsilon_P\circ\beta_{P,P^\vee}\circ(h\otimes1_{P^\vee})\circ(g\otimes1_{P^\vee})\circ\eta_P=\varepsilon_P\circ\beta_{P,P^\vee}\circ(h\otimes t)\circ\eta_Q.$$
Here $(h\otimes1_{P^\vee})\circ(1_Q\otimes t)=h\otimes t$, so the replacement is well typed through $Q\otimes P^\vee$.

source.place: Part (3), final sentence invoking conjugacy invariance; explicit agent expansion of the dual-mate calculation in lean/WeilConjectures/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Rigid/Braided.lean:80–96.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-braiding-naturality] to $h:Q\to P$ and $t:Q^\vee\to P^\vee$, obtaining $\beta_{P,P^\vee}\circ(h\otimes t)=(t\otimes h)\circ\beta_{Q,Q^\vee}$. Factor $t\otimes h=(t\otimes1_P)\circ(1_{Q^\vee}\otimes h)$ and use the evaluation equation from [lem-zl-right-dual-mate-identities]. Thus the expression in step 3 equals
$$\varepsilon_Q\circ(1_{Q^\vee}\otimes g)\circ(1_{Q^\vee}\otimes h)\circ\beta_{Q,Q^\vee}\circ\eta_Q=\varepsilon_Q\circ(1_{Q^\vee}\otimes(g\circ h))\circ\beta_{Q,Q^\vee}\circ\eta_Q.$$
Both substitutions use only tensor bifunctoriality and associativity.

source.place: Part (3), final sentence invoking conjugacy invariance; explicit agent expansion of the dual-mate calculation in lean/WeilConjectures/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Rigid/Braided.lean:80–96.

proof.text: Naturality [lem-sfb-braiding-naturality], now with $g\circ h:Q\to Q$ and $1_{Q^\vee}$, rewrites $(1_{Q^\vee}\otimes(g\circ h))\circ\beta_{Q,Q^\vee}$ as $\beta_{Q,Q^\vee}\circ((g\circ h)\otimes1_{Q^\vee})$. Since $g\circ h=v$ by step 1, the resulting composite is $\varepsilon_Q\circ\beta_{Q,Q^\vee}\circ(v\otimes1_{Q^\vee})\circ\eta_Q=\operatorname{tr}(v)$ by [sk-d-trace]. All equalities are morphism equalities $\mathbf1\to\mathbf1$, proving the assertion.
